newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - APRIL 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - APRIL 3.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--Greece has come to the forefront of diplomatic activity to find a way out of the Albaian impasse, with Athens hosting a quadrilateral meeting today between Albanian Prime Minister Bashkim Fino, Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos, OSCE envoy Franz Vranitsky and Dutch Foreign Minister and EU Council of Ministers President Hans Van Mierlo.
--Prime Minister Costas Simitis told Fino yesterday that Athens' concerns over the ethnic Greek minority in the south were in no way geared towards creating a 'zone of influence'.

--Voluntary retirement for 3,000 employees of the Greek telecoms organisation, OTE, will help in curbing OTE's 140 billion drachma annual wage bill. OTE hopes some 5,000 employees close to retirement will take up the offer.
--Simitis is pleased with the 'steady improvement in economic indices' he told ruling party PASOK MPs yesterday, warning however that the work had to continue.
--Minority schools in neighbouring Turkey - 28 Greek, 45 Armenian and six Jewish - face closure if new government legislation goes through.
--The quadrilateral meeting on Albania scheduled for Athens today will coordinate moves for a solution to the neighbouring country's crisis.
--A young woman was found brutally stabbed to death in her downtown Athens apartment yesterday. The grisly discovery was made by the 19-year-old girl's mother.

--Only through free elections can Albania find its way out of the morass, Albania's Socialist Party leader Fatos Nano says. Albanian President Sali Berisha's task, he adds, is to prepare the ground for elections and not meddle in politics: the Fino government is the only guarantee at this moment.

--The new wage payment system for civil servants via bank accounts will also provide an opportunity for supervisory authorities to check whether employees are receiving overpayments or bonuses they are not entitled to.

--Staggered opening hours - designed to reduce traffic converging on the city centre as well as air pollution - will be applied again this summer, Environment, Town Planning and Public Works Minister Costas Laliotis plans.

--New Democracy president Costas Karamanlis's first appearance as leader of the conservative opposition party to the party's MPs yesterday was a resounding success and bodes well for his determination to keep the party unified. Noted at the meeting was a smiling Constantine Mitsotakis, former leader and premier, sitting next to former arch foe, Miltiades Evert, the loser in recent leadership elections.
--The Workers Housing Organisation is to increase subsidies and benefits for young families and low wage-earners and pension earners.
